issue.title: Seekable playback: convert committed AAC take to M4A for Review scrubbing
issue.body:
## Summary

The Record Tab Review state (#49) requires scrubbing the draft waveform to any position. Recording commits takes as **ADTS AAC (`.aac`)**, which is not reliably seekable, so #49 **waives** the scrubbing acceptance criterion and defers it here to be solved and reviewed separately.

This issue covers both halves of the problem: the **commit format** and the **scrubbing** it needs to enable.

## Background / why the format is the way it is

Recording captures into **ADTS AAC (`.aac`)** rather than the preset `.m4a` on purpose (see `src/hooks/useRecorder.ts`):

- An MP4/M4A file is only valid once its `moov` atom is written on a clean `stop()`. A process kill mid-recording leaves it unplayable and un-appendable.
- ADTS is a self-framing stream: a killed segment stays playable, and multiple segments concatenate by byte-append. This is what makes **pause / resume-after-kill** possible.

The trade-off: ADTS AAC has **no container index / `moov` atom**, so accurate absolute seeking (scrubbing) is unreliable. We do not want to give up kill-safe resumable capture to get seeking, so the two formats must coexist.

## Current vs expected

- **Current:** committed takes are stored as ADTS `.aac`. Playback works, but scrubbing to an arbitrary position is not reliably accurate.
- **Expected:** Review can scrub to any position accurately, reading from a **seekable** file, without regressing resumable capture.

## Proposed approach

Build a **local (native) module** — an Expo local/native module or config-plugin-backed module, since this is CNG / Android-only — that, after a take is committed, **converts/remuxes the committed ADTS `.aac` into an M4A (MP4/AAC) file** with a proper `moov` atom.

- Keep ADTS AAC as the **capture/resume** format (do not regress kill-safe resumable takes).
- Run the AAC → M4A conversion as part of / immediately after commit (`commitRecording` in `src/hooks/useRecorder.ts`), and resolve the committed take's playable URI to the M4A output.
- Feed the seekable M4A into the existing playback/seek path (`src/hooks/useAudioPlayback.ts`) that backs the Review scrub UI (`src/app/tabs/drafting/record/components/RecordingWaveform.tsx`).

## Scope

**In scope**
- Local native module to convert/remux a committed AAC take to seekable M4A.
- Wiring the converted M4A into the commit flow and playback URI resolution.
- Accurate scrubbing in the Review state on the converted file.

**Out of scope**
- Changing the capture/resume format (stays ADTS AAC).
- Waveform amplitude generation / visual design beyond enabling accurate seek.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A committed take is converted to a seekable M4A (MP4/AAC) file after commit.
- [ ] Review-state scrubbing seeks accurately to arbitrary positions on the converted file (satisfies the #49-waived scrubbing AC).
- [ ] Capture, pause, and resume-after-kill continue to work unchanged (still ADTS AAC).
- [ ] Conversion failure is handled gracefully (logged; take remains playable even if non-seekable) — no data loss.
- [ ] Android device QA recorded on the PR (native module + audio path).

## Verification / test plan

- Unit-test the commit → convert → resolve-URI path (mock the native module).
- Android device QA: record a take, commit, then scrub the Review waveform to multiple positions and confirm playback resumes accurately from each.

## File pointers

- `src/hooks/useRecorder.ts` — AAC/ADTS capture decision (comment near the `useAudioRecorder` config) and `commitRecording`.
- `src/hooks/useAudioPlayback.ts` — `seek()` / playback used by Review.
- `src/app/tabs/drafting/record/components/RecordingWaveform.tsx` — Review scrub UI (`onSeek`, `durationMs`).
- `app.config.ts` / `plugins/` — where a local native module / config plugin would be wired (CNG, Android-only).

## Links

Refs #49
Related: #96 (playback engine + waveform decision)

comments.body:
## Spike #176 — findings: m4a vs ADTS capture (bounded, ~half day)

Ran the bounded kill-test spike on a physical Android device (dev client). TL;DR: **there is no single crash-safe *and* natively-seekable capture format available through an `expo-audio` preset**, which confirms ADTS capture is the right call. Two real options remain for producing a seekable take (below) — flagging before any more native code per the ask.

### 1. Default `HIGH_QUALITY` `.m4a` (`mpeg4`) preset — kill mid-take
**Result: lossy on crash.** After a mid-take force-kill, only a **prefix** of the take is playable; audio recorded near the moment of the kill is lost. MediaRecorder streams samples into `mdat` while recording but only finalizes the `moov` (sample index) on a clean `stop()`, so a killed take has a missing/stale index and can't recover the tail. (Exact symptom can vary by device/player — open-with-prefix vs fail-to-open — but it's lossy either way.)

Video:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28aab85b-c027-41d6-b6cf-ce95a38cc4c0


### 2. Our ADTS config (`aac_adts` / `.aac`) — kill mid-take
**Result: fully playable + resumable.** The partial take plays end-to-end after a kill, because every AAC frame is self-framing (no central index to go stale). This is what makes byte-append concatenation and resume-after-kill work.

Video: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21439538-5d3b-4417-900b-a31daeb6854e

### 3. Output formats exposed by `expo-audio`
`AndroidOutputFormat` is fixed to: `default | 3gp | mpeg4 | amrnb | amrwb | aac_adts | mpeg2ts | webm`. **No fragmented-MP4 (fMP4) option.** Of these, only `aac_adts` and `mpeg2ts` are self-framing / crash-tolerant; none are both crash-safe **and** natively seekable via a preset. (Confirmed by inspecting the shipped types — no device needed.)

### 4. Fragmented MP4
As predicted, fMP4 (`moof`/`mdat` fragments) is **not reachable through a preset**. Getting it would require a custom `AudioRecord → MediaCodec → fragmented muxer` pipeline — a much larger native project than the remux module. **Ruled out for this feature.**

### Conclusion
No single-format path through `expo-audio` gives us crash-safety + native seek. ADTS capture stands. That leaves the two valid options called out in the ticket for turning captured ADTS into a seekable take:

- **B — ADTS capture + remux on commit:** losslessly repackage the merged ADTS into a seekable `.m4a` via Android `MediaMuxer` (`AacRemux`). Not brute force — it's the platform API JS can't reach.
- **A — segment manifest + global seek in playback (JS only):** keep the ordered ADTS segments, play them as one logical stream, map global position → `(segment, offset)`. No Kotlin.

The A-vs-B decision hinges on **intra-ADTS seek accuracy** and **cross-segment boundary smoothness**, which I have *not* measured yet.

### Scope flag before more native code
Holding here per "post findings before building any more native code" — **how do you want to proceed?**
- (b) go straight to Option B (keep the remux) and delete the Option A prototype, or
- (c) merge-at-sync/server and play a single file.

## Append: fMP4 findings — why we're not taking that path

fMP4 (fragmented MP4) is the one container that is *both* crash-safe and seekable:
an init segment (`ftyp` + skeletal `moov`) is written up front, then each fragment
(`moof` index + `mdat` audio) is self-describing — so flushed fragments stay playable
after a kill, and each carries a sample table for precise seek. It would collapse both
concerns the ADTS+remux path splits (crash-safe capture vs. seekable playback) into a
single file, retiring `AacRemux`.

It is reachable natively: `androidx.media3.muxer.FragmentedMp4Muxer`
(`setFragmentDurationMs`, default 2000ms) produces fMP4. But **not through `expo-audio`**
— `AndroidOutputFormat` exposes no fMP4, so this means replacing the recorder with a
custom `AudioRecord → MediaCodec → FragmentedMp4Muxer` pipeline.

Why we're **not** doing it now:

- **Much larger than the remux module.** We'd own raw mic capture, AAC encode, the
  muxer, a **foreground-service** (`microphone` FGS type) lifecycle, and metering —
  everything `expo-audio` currently handles for us.
- **Crash-recovery is not free.** A kill can leave a torn trailing fragment, so we'd
  need a relaunch **repair/truncate** step. More importantly, media3 writes samples "in
  batches," so the real loss window depends on **disk-flush cadence** — unverified, and
  the single biggest risk to prove before trusting the crash-safety claim.
- **Doesn't remove multi-segment.** `FragmentedMp4Muxer` can't be reopened to append, so
  resume-after-kill still yields N files — same as ADTS today — and fMP4 files don't
  byte-concatenate (each has its own init segment), so merging needs a real remux pass.

**Decision:** stay on crash-safe ADTS capture; the A-vs-B choice (JS manifest vs.
ADTS→M4A remux) is unchanged. fMP4 is the theoretically ideal format but a disproportionate
native subsystem for this feature. Revisit only if a future ticket needs a single
crash-safe + seekable artifact and is scoped for a dedicated native recorder — first step
would be a throwaway spike that records fragments, hard-kills the process, and **measures
the actual tail loss** to validate the flush window.

[fluent-mobile-176-spike.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29986390/fluent-mobile-176-spike.zip)

## Device test update — Option C (m4a segments + manifest + global seek)

Reran the final device test with **Record .m4a + Keep manifest + Segment playback** forced on, killing the app **two ways**: Recents swipe *and* `adb shell am force-stop com.eten.fluent` (system-style kill).

> 📹 Screen recording attached below.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32480d56-7455-4675-aff4-3635c9138013

### What worked
- **Gap-free sequential playback** across multiple independently-finalized `.m4a` segments — little to no perceptible gap at boundaries.
- **Accurate global seek** across the whole take: maps to the right 


segment and the correct offset within it (relative to total duration), auto-switching `.m4a` files while scrubbing.
- **No native remux needed** — each `.m4a` is self-seekable (own `moov`/sample table), so `manifest + useSegmentedAudioPlayback` plays N files as one logical, seekable stream.
- Contrary to the step-1 kill test and the documented "no `moov` on abrupt kill," **most** hard kills (swipe *and* `am force-stop`) left the in-flight segment playable — likely because expo-audio releases/finalizes the recorder on teardown and the muxer runs in a separate media-server process.

### Downsides
- `.m4a` segments are **not reliably mergeable into one file in JS** (MP4 is a box structure; would need ffmpeg/native).
- In-flight crash-safety is **best-effort, not guaranteed** — **some** runs still produced a corrupt (moov-less) segment. It's timing/OEM-dependent, so it can't be leaned on for data safety. The manifest writer drops any moov-less segment (probe → 0ms), so the failure mode degrades to "lose the last chunk," never "whole take unplayable." ADTS remains the only *guaranteed* crash-safe capture.

I also tried to reproduce the "corrupt state" locally more aggressively (using the CLI `am force-stop` to match how Android actually kills the app) and it happens **less often** than the docs/research imply — though frequency is still unknown.

### Recommendation — depends on how reliable we need crash recovery to be
- **If occasional unrecoverable in-flight chunks are acceptable → Option C, with a recovery prompt.** When the in-flight segment can't be recovered, tell the user that chunk couldn't be saved and prompt them to re-record it. Given how hard the corruption has been to reproduce in practice, this is my lean — but it's a product/reliability call, not purely technical.
- **If we need near-guaranteed recovery → don't ship C as-is.** Either stay on **Option B** (ADTS + `MediaMuxer` remux, or merge at sync/server) for guaranteed crash-safe capture + accurate seek, or invest in a merge/repair step before relying on m4a segments.

A/B/C stays **deferred pending the tech-lead call** per this issue — no native code deleted or graduated. The Option A/C prototype (`useSegmentedAudioPlayback`, manifest writer/resolver, runtime debug flags, MP4/ADTS duration probes) is all on `fel-cesar/spike/explore-m4a` for side-by-side comparison.

**Assignee cleared** — `fel-cesar` is no longer on the project.

Related recording PRs closed (do not merge): #158, #178, #184. Branches remain as reference/salvage only.

This issue stays open. Re-assign when someone intentionally picks it up; prefer thin PRs against current `main` rather than reviving the closed mega-diffs.
Status corrected: moved from In PR Review → Dev Ready. Closed Cesar PRs (#158/#178/#184) are not under review; this card is available to pick up as a thin PR from current main.

## AC waiver (AGENTS.md) — native remux deferred

PR #231 lands the **JS remux seam only** (`ensureSeekableTakeUri` + optional native inject). It does **not** implement the Android `MediaMuxer` remux module or complete #176 scrubbing AC.

**Waived pending follow-up #233:**
- [ ] Committed take converted to seekable M4A after commit (native remux)
- [ ] Review scrubbing accurate on converted file
- [ ] Android device QA for native remux + audio path

**Satisfied / not blocked by this waiver:**
- Conversion failure / missing module → take stays playable AAC (no data loss) — covered by the JS seam
- Capture/pause/resume-after-kill format unchanged by #231

**Follow-up:** #233 — native AAC→M4A remux module + device QA.

Do **not** treat `Closes #176` on #231 as full AC completion; #176 stays open until #233 lands (or AC is otherwise met).

## SP1 queue update — Review scrub UX shipped; #176 stays open for #233

PR #252 (stacked on #105 / #251) wires the **Review scrub surface**:
- Tap/drag on draft waveform → `useVerseAudio.seek`
- Playback engine `load()` so scrub works before play
- Works today on HIGH_QUALITY `.m4a`; ADTS remux still missing

**Does not close #176** (per prior waiver): native MediaMuxer remux + accurate scrub on remuxed ADTS + device QA remain **#233**.

Next queue item after #252 CI: **#233**.

### Why this issue stays open
